mainEntity.name: Should I use one master prompt or several specialized AI assistants?

acceptedAnswer.text:
The right number of prompts depends on your workflow, not the size of a library. Start with one assistant for one defined job, then add another only when the first process is stable and a clear handoff exists.

Context: The 38 Bot Empire resource contains examples across planning, research, content, marketing, sales, websites, and operations, but the collection is a library of adaptable blueprints rather than 38 identical software products. Run My AI Business recommends focused implementation.

Key factors:
- How many recurring workflows you actually use.
- Whether each assistant has a distinct responsibility.
- The effort required to maintain context and outputs.
- Your ability to review the combined process.

Practical guidance: Begin with one prompt for a priority workflow, document the result, and add a second only when it receives reliable inputs. Use a central brief to keep audience, offer, voice, and deadlines consistent.

A smaller, well-maintained system is often more useful than a large unused collection.
acceptedAnswer.description: Start with one specialized assistant for a priority workflow. Add more only when the first process is reliable and each new assistant has a distinct role, clear inputs, and a defined handoff. A large prompt library is not automatically better.
